en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2).
20.3. Āsavagocchaka.
Dependent on a state that is not associated with cankers (*anāsava*), a state associated with cankers (*āsava*) arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is not associated with cankers, a state not associated with cankers (*anoāsava*) arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is not associated with cankers, states both associated with cankers and not associated with cankers arise by way of the root condition. … [Three.]
Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, a state that is an *āsava* arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, states that are both *āsava* and not an *āsava* arise by way of the root condition. … [three].

Dependent on a state that is both with-outflows (*sāsava*) and not-with-outflows (*anāsava*), a state with-outflows arises by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). ... [Three] (Abbreviated). Nine under the root-condition ... pe ...
one under the result-condition (*vipāka*) ... pe ... nine under the non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*).
Dependent on a state that is not-with-outflows, a state with-outflows arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that is not-with-outflows ... [text continues]
Dependent on a state that is not subject to cankers (anāsava), a state that is not subject to cankers arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to cankers, states both subject to cankers (sāsava) and not subject to cankers arise by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is not subject to cankers, a state subject to cankers arises by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is both with taints (*sāsava*) and not with taints (*anāsava*), a state with taints arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). … One. (Abbreviated.
Under the root condition there are five … pe … under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two … pe … under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are five.
Dependent on a state associated with taints (*āsavasampayutta*), a state associated with taints arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, six … pe … in the ripening condition, one … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, nine.

Dependent on a state that is both with-outflows (*sāsava*) and without-outflows (*anāsava*), there arises a state that is both with-outflows and without-outflows by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
In the case of the root condition, there are nine … pe … in the ripening condition, one … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, nine.

Dependent on a state that is both with-outflows (*āsava*) and dissociated from outflows, there arises a state that is both with-outflows and associated with outflows, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine [conditions] in the case of the root; ... pe ... nine in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from outflows and without-outflows (*anāsava*), there arises a state that is dissociated from outflows but with-outflows, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two ... [and so on] ... in the non-disappearance condition, there are five.
